answer.main_body: desert bush foliage and base stems
answer.evidence: The bush is drawn as a flat side-view sprite typical of a 2D platformer. The four brown stem legs at the bottom (rows 12-14) stand in a straight horizontal line, allowing the viewer to look straight underneath the bush horizontally rather than looking down from a 45-degree angle. The foliage silhouette is a purely vertical side profile with no foreshortened top surface.

The bush is drawn in a flat side-view/platformer elevation. All ground contact stems terminate along the same horizontal baseline (row 13) without depth separation, and the foliage is rendered as a flat vertical silhouette with 2D lighting rather than foreshortened top-down volume.

The bush is drawn as a flat 2D side/front silhouette with an upper lobe (cloud-like silhouette) rather than a foreshortened top surface seen from above. Furthermore, all four base stems terminate along the exact same horizontal baseline (row 13), typical of a side-scroller front elevation.
The bush canopy displays a top surface across rows 3-5 with top-down lighting and curvature, transitioning into the front face below down to the base stems at row 13.
